clue.text: Colour question re urge to mingle

indicators.note: things that mingle mix together freely, so the three words before are blended into a new order

parts.note: the three words taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone is asked about an urge to go out and socialise.
explanation.walkthrough: All fourteen letters of the three middle words are rearranged; nothing is added or lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Turquoise green is a named shade, a bluish green, so it is one example of a colour.

clue.text: Globe, perhaps, to which actors hie, thunder ''n'' rotate wildly

indicators.note: doing something wildly means doing it in disorder, so the preceding words are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: hie, thunder, the n of 'n' and rotate, seventeen letters in all

explanation.surface: Actors hurry to the Globe, thundering about and spinning around in excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: Hie is an old word for hurry, and it belongs to the fodder even though it reads as part of the definition's sentence. This answer runs on into 6-down.
explanation.definitionFit: The Globe on London's South Bank is a circular playhouse with the audience on all sides, an example of that staging arrangement.

clue.text: Wine jar smashed around 10

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters are placed on either side of what follows
a smashed jar is broken into pieces, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then mixed
the number 10 read as its two digits, which look like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A wine jar has been broken, perhaps near clue 10.
explanation.walkthrough: The 10 looks like a cross-reference to 10-down, but it is simply the digits 1 and 0 used as the letters I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white wine from the Spanish region of La Rioja, so it is a named type of wine.

clue.text: How poker players might punt with heat and energy

indicators.note: might hints that the letters could just as well appear in some other order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Card players placing bets heatedly and energetically.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no strong mixing word; the clue reads almost as a description of the action, and punt, heat and E simply share the answer's nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To up the ante is to raise the stake in poker, which is the way players increase what each must bet.

clue.text: Considering chains of arraignment arresting

indicators.note: arresting means seizing and holding, so the words before hold the answer inside them

parts.note: the run of letters across the end of chains, all of of, and the start of arraignment

explanation.surface: Thinking about the chains used when a prisoner is brought into court and charged.
explanation.definitionFit: Insofar (as) introduces the extent or ground of a claim, much as considering does when weighing a point.

clue.text: 18! 18 the Spanish that's good for Madame

indicators.note: the second cross-reference to 18-down means raise, and raising letters in a down entry turns them upside down

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
the French for good in its feminine form, as a madame would be described

explanation.surface: A cryptic chain of cross-references with a French lady thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 18-down is ELEVATE, used twice: first as the definition, then as an instruction to raise the letters. ELBONNE read upwards gives ENNOBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble someone is to raise them to the peerage, so it is a form of elevating them in rank.

clue.text: See 1
Androgynous duo with refined niche development

indicators.note: a development is a change of form, so the collected letters take on a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
U is old slang for upper-class, hence refined
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gender-neutral pair develops a refined market niche.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from Nancy Mitford's 'U and non-U' usage and is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Eunuchoid describes someone with features like those of a eunuch, lacking strong male traits, close to androgynous in sense.

clue.text: Reservists given order to return with some craft

indicators.note: returning means going back the way one came, so the combined letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
Order of the British Empire, an honour

explanation.surface: Reserve soldiers are ordered back, taking some boats with them.
explanation.walkthrough: TA plus OBE gives TAOBE, which read backwards is EBOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An E-boat was a German fast motor torpedo boat of the Second World War, a particular kind of vessel.

clue.text: That hopeful fan of Sir Edward Elgar

definitions.note: a title reference, the word that names Elgar's fan
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Elgar's 1917 ballet is called The ____ Fan

explanation.surface: An optimistic admirer of the composer Elgar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' looks like an enthusiast, but it is the literal fan in the title of Elgar's ballet The Sanguine Fan.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanguine means optimistic and confident about the future, a close synonym of hopeful.

clue.text: What Christians celebrate madly in a second, say

indicators.note: acting madly means acting without order, so the following words are jumbled

parts.note: the four words taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Christians celebrate wildly in an instant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascension Day is the Christian feast forty days after Easter marking Christ's rising into heaven, a festival the faithful keep.

clue.text: Thief seeing some fortune in this?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Cockney rhyming slang, rhyming with thief
second meaning: what a fortune-teller reads in the bottom of a cup

explanation.surface: A thief who sees riches in the loot.
explanation.walkthrough: Fortune looks like money a thief is after; it is the future, read in the dregs of a teacup. Rhyming slang replaces a word with a phrase that rhymes with it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang a thief is a tea leaf, and tasseography reads the future from the leaves left in a cup.

clue.text: City knights coming from bedclothes

parts.note: only the front half of this word is wordplay, taken as written; the back half is the definition
EC is the postcode of the City of London
K is the chess abbreviation for king's knight; plural for two

explanation.surface: Knights of the City of London rising from their bedclothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bedclothes' must be split: bed is wordplay, and clothes, as a verb, is the definition. City with a capital means the financial district of London.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedeck is to adorn or dress up, so bedecks works as a verb meaning dresses or clothes.

clue.text: Nigel's behaving oddly; could he be losing his marbles?

definitions.text: could he be losing his marbles?

indicators.note: behaving oddly means acting out of the normal order, so the name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name taken as written

explanation.surface: Nigel's strange behaviour makes people wonder if he is going mad.
explanation.walkthrough: Losing his marbles looks like going senile; it refers to the Elgin Marbles, the Parthenon sculptures Lord Elgin removed and which Greece wants returned.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Elgin brought the Parthenon sculptures to Britain, and Greek demands for their return would see him losing those statues.

clue.text: Golden Ass, going East for one, could be on the slide

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might form something else once rearranged
going says one letter leaves the title
x for y means swap in a replacement where the departing letter stood

parts.note: the title of Apuleius's Latin novel, taken as written
the compass abbreviation; this letter goes
the Roman numeral for one comes in

explanation.surface: A classical novel, sent eastward in exchange, might be in decline.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the E of Golden Ass for I to get GOLDINASS, then rearrange. 'On the slide' sounds like decline, but here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A glissando is a musical slide, a rapid run up or down the scale played by sliding the finger.

clue.text: One reverses current false report about man with nothing

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the twisted letters wrap round what follows
a false account is a distorted one, so the next word's letters are twisted

parts.note: taken as written, then mixed
he is the pronoun for a man
the zero-shaped letter

explanation.surface: Someone contradicts a mistaken story about a man who has nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Current is electrical, not topical; reverses has nothing to do with turning letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: A rheotrope is an old electrical device, a commutator, that switches the direction of flow in a circuit.

clue.text: Dog food container found on the back of a lorry

definitions.text: found on the back of a lorry

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely, to tail them
a board is a table laid for a meal, as in the festive board

explanation.surface: A tin of pet food spotted on the back of a truck.
explanation.walkthrough: Dog food container reads as a pet-food tin; Dog is a verb, and the board is the table food is set out on. 'Fell off the back of a lorry' is British slang for stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailboard is the hinged flap at the rear of a lorry or cart that drops down for loading.

clue.text: Gray's tenor doesn't sing

definitions.note: a quotation: the adjective Gray gives the tenor
definitions.meaning: first meaning: Thomas Gray's Elegy says villagers kept the quiet tenor of their way, tenor meaning course

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the adjective silent
definitions.meaning: second meaning: making no sound at all

explanation.surface: A tenor called Gray stays silent.
explanation.walkthrough: Tenor here is a course of life, not a voice. Gray's Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard has the line 'They kept the noiseless tenor of their way'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that makes no sound is silent, the epithet Gray attached to the even course of humble lives.

clue.text: Uplifted English rose wine village with European advance

indicators.note: lifting letters upward in a down entry means reading them from bottom to top

parts.note: the standard abbreviation
Tavel, in the Rhone valley, is famous for rose wine
the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: An English rose and wine from a French village, enjoyed as Europe progresses.
explanation.walkthrough: Rose is rosé, pink wine, not the flower; English rose looks like a phrase but splits in two. ETAVELE read upwards gives ELEVATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate someone is to promote or raise them in rank, the same as advancing them.

clue.text: How long can you stay with this?

definitions.text: How long can you stay with this?

parts.words: How long can you stay with this?
parts.note: surface reading: a question about the length of a visit
setter's reading: stay means endure, so this is the quality that lets you keep going

explanation.walkthrough: Stay sounds like lodging somewhere; in the sense of staying power it means lasting the distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is endurance, the physical capacity to sustain effort over a long period.

clue.text: One taking a course might attempt to get off work

indicators.note: getting off means leaving, so this part departs from the larger word

parts.note: industry is hard work, diligence
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A student on a course trying to skip work.
explanation.walkthrough: One taking a course looks like a student; it is a river following its course. Work is a noun meaning diligence, not a job.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus is a great river of Pakistan, and rivers are things that follow a course.

clue.text: Behan's work hot 1 6 down? On the contrary!

indicators.note: the cross-reference asks for one thing set within another; the contrary flips which surrounds which

parts.note: H for hot, as on a tap
1-down begins with theatre, and a stage stands for the theatre
6-down is the word round, and the round letter is O

explanation.surface: Is Behan's play a hot ticket in a circular theatre? Quite the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: Hot theatre in the round would put H STAGE inside O; on the contrary, O goes inside H STAGE. Brendan Behan's play The Hostage dates from 1958.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hostage is a play by the Irish writer Brendan Behan, so it is one of his works.

clue.text: Tree hiding hairless old African warriors

indicators.note: the suffix less means without, so the hair is taken away from the warriors

parts.note: the Matabele, or Ndebele, were a 19th-century warrior people of southern Africa
a mat is a thick tangle of hair

explanation.surface: A tree conceals a band of bald veteran fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: Hairless has to be split: hair is what goes and less is the instruction. Hiding just joins the tree to the remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The abele is the white poplar, a species of tree with silvery leaves.

clue.text: Where Italians accommodate Lulu's man without proscription — nothing!

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the next word's letters are removed

parts.note: Alban Berg, composer of the opera Lulu
a ban is a proscription
the zero-shaped letter

explanation.surface: Where Italians put up a singer's man, with no restrictions at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Lulu looks like the pop singer; she is the heroine of Berg's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Albergo is the Italian word for an inn or hotel, a place where people in Italy are given lodging.

clue.text: Unyielding soldier gaining free entry

indicators.note: gaining means taking something in, so the next word acquires the soldier inside it
an entry is a way in, confirming the soldier goes inside

parts.note: to free of something is to rid of it
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A stubborn soldier gets in without paying.
explanation.walkthrough: Free entry looks like admission without charge; the soldier is the one gaining entry into the word for free.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid describes something stiff that will not bend, the same as unyielding.

clue.text: A troublesome tenant, one of those born before the event

indicators.note: something troublesome causes disorder, so its letters are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A difficult lodger, one who arrived before something happened.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'one of' reads as part of the definition, but one supplies the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Antenati is a legal and historical term for people born before a given date, such as a change in law or national independence.

clue.text: Hibernal, giddy with cold

indicators.note: with here means containing, so the preceding words carry the answer inside them

parts.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Wintry and dizzy from the chill.
explanation.walkthrough: Hibernal looks like the definition, since it means wintry, but it is part of the hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: Algid is a rare, formal word for chilly or cold, from the Latin algidus.

clue.text: How long will our love last? Watch out for the gallery, Robin!

definitions.text: How long will our love last?

parts.note: the golfer's warning shout
a veranda is a roofed gallery along the outside of a house
Sir Robin Day, the British television political interviewer

explanation.surface: A lover asks how long it will last, then warns Robin about the gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin looks like a bird or a lover's name; it is Sir Robin Day, the famous BBC political interviewer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means eternally, the romantic answer to a question about how long love will endure.
